translation_notes: prefixes: OWL->owl, XMLNS->xmlns, XSD->xsd, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs
kg is created once per call and never reassigned, so a single @graph kg before the loop is enough; every kg.add(...) becomes +{ }.

each if-guarded triple stays its own +{ } (one add per condition); the two runs of consecutive unconditional adds (Name/label, then populationServed/serviceConnections/hasActivity) merge into one +{ s p1 o1 ; p2 o2 } each, and the CDS pair merges into one +{ s1 a T . s2 p s1 } block, all matching the source's shared-subject grouping without changing which triples are conditional.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `prefixes['us_sdwis']` is read once into `us_sdwis` before the loop, and its fixed terms use attribute access (`us_sdwis.pwsName`, the same Namespace term). `iris['PWS']` becomes `pws_iri`, `'X' in pws.keys()` becomes `'X' in pws`, and `str('PublicWaterSystem' + '-' + x)` becomes `'PublicWaterSystem-' + x`.

optimized.py, restructuring: the five unconditional triples (base type, population, connections, activity, firstReport, moved up beside the others) are one `kg += [...]`. The Transient and GWSW subtypes share one `for key in (...)` loop, and the Type != "NP" test keeps its own if. The five optional literal properties (pwsName and rdfs:label of Name, Deactivation, Owner, LastReport) become one table `(key, predicate, datatype)` read by one `if key in pws: kg.add(...)`. The CDS pair is one `kg += [...]`. Every condition of the original is kept with the same test. kg is local and is lost if an exception propagates, so moving the writes changes no observable state.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph kg`, one `+{ }` with `;` for the unconditional block, `{x}^^xsd:int|string|date` for the typed literals (it transpiles to the same `Literal(x, datatype=...)`), and `{pws[key]}^^{datatype}` in the table loop, whose datatypes and rdfs:label are prefixed names. `@prefix xsd:` is declared at the top of the function because the extracted header is not to be touched. us_sdwis stays a runtime Namespace (it comes from the `prefixes` dict, which also feeds the graph's bindings): declaring its IRI as a second `@prefix` would duplicate it, just as a Python `Namespace("...")` would.
No exception to the symmetry rule: every restructuring (alias, table, loop, merge) is on both sides.
header_optimization_notes: optimized_header.py: OWL, XMLNS, URIRef and BNode go, all unused. XSD, RDF, RDFS, Literal and the four shim names stay.

optimized_header.ldpy: both rdflib import lines go: XSD, RDF, RDFS and Literal are replaced by xsd:/`a`/rdfs:/typed literals, and the rest are unused. The header's `@prefix rdfs:` is used. `@prefix xsd:` sits in the region and stays there.
